newsitem.title: USA: U.S. agency declares forest fires under control.
newsitem.headline: U.S. agency declares forest fires under control.

text.p: All major wildfires in national forests that had been blazing in the West and Southeast were out or under control on Wednesday, the U.S. Forest Service said.
"Early rains in the Pacific Northwest have helped us get control of what had become a very busy wildfire season," Forest Service chief Jack Ward Thomas said.
The near-record wildfire season saw almost six million acres of grasslands, forests and private lands scorched, the agency said. Most of the damage was on private lands.

Fires on National Forest System lands accounted for more than 10 percent of the 89,000 wildfires, with most of the damage sustained in the Pacific Northwest. National forests in the Southeast suffered less harm partly because the forest service had used controlled fires to remove dead and dying trees to ease the threat of wildfires there, Thomas said.
"It is cheaper to manage fires than to wait until they are out of control and then try to suppress them," he said.
U.S. agencies have spent more than $400 million battling fires this year, the forest service said. The fire season was expected to continue in California and the Southeast.
